newsitem.title: FRANCE: PRESS DIGEST - France - Le Monde April 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - France - Le Monde April 18.

text.p: These are leading stories in today's afternoon daily Le Monde, dated April 19.

-- A number of prominent politicians are convinced that President Jacques Chirac will dissolve parliament and call early elections. Growing budget deficit requires higher payroll taxes or deep cuts into health care, welfare and other government spending.
-- U.N. envoy Mohamed Sahnoun says President Mobutu Sese Seko may meet opponent Laurent Desire Kabila "very soon".
-- Former prime minister Michel Rocard warns NATO not to jeopardise Russia's ratification of Start II or to push the country into re-arming.
-- World Health Organisation panel recommends formally listing nicotine as a controlled substance, a move that could lead to nicotine-free cigarettes if approved.

-- Top 25 French corporations earned total profits of 43.6 billion francs in 1996 against 8.1 billion in 1995, but lag behind their global competitors in size, financial muscle and international presence.
-- EU Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert says Boeing deals with Delta and American airlines may amount to restrictive marketing practises.

-- SNCF chairman Emmanuel Han says Moody's move to drop SNCF railways' long-term debt rating from Aaa to Aa1 is "incomprehensible" and based on "purely ideological" speculation that assumes eventual privatisation. SNCF expects the Aa1 rating to cost it an extra 40 million francs per year.
-- Bank of France says "no comment" to queries about 1,000 lay-offs.
